description.narrative:
IFCs long-term financing is expected to enhance access to housing and climate finance in Peru by supporting BanBifs mortgage lending to women-led households and expanding its green building portfolio. The Project will promote greater financial inclusion by enabling more women to access housing finance and by fostering equitable participation in the housing market.
Beyond the project-level impact, IFC anticipates that the transaction will strengthen the local market for sustainable housing finance by accelerating BanBifs strategy to expand green building finance and encouraging wider adoption of EDGE or equivalent certifications. By supporting both developer finance and green mortgages, the Project is expected to contribute to the availability of quality, climate-resilient housing and generate environmental co-benefits through greater energy and water efficiency.

The proposed investment is an up to US$150 million financing package for Banco Interamericano de Finanzas S.A. (BanBif or the Bank), consisting of senior and subordinated debt. Senior debt includes a five-year amortizable senior loan of up to US$100 million, with a three-year grace period, out of which IFC's will invest up to US$70 million on its own account. Subordinated debt is a 10 years and three months bullet bond of up to US$50 million, with a call option in year five. The financing package aims to: (i) support the financing of green and other sustainable projects of the Bank (iii) strengthen the Bank's regulatory capital base to support its growth (the Project)
